info.text: A eukaryotic cell is not a bag of interchangeable parts: membranes regulate exchange, genetic information is selectively used, and organelles divide production, transport, energy conversion, and recycling into coordinated compartments.

citations.title: Eukaryotic Cells
citations.author: Mary Ann Clark, Matthew Douglas, and Jung Choi

citations.title: Passive Transport
citations.author: Mary Ann Clark, Matthew Douglas, and Jung Choi

clusters.name: Boundary and exchange
clusters.fact: The plasma membrane is a selectively permeable phospholipid bilayer whose channels and receptors regulate movement and communication across the cell boundary.

clusters.name: Information and control
clusters.fact: The nucleus houses chromosomes, while transcription selectively copies genomic information into RNA for use elsewhere in the cell.

clusters.name: Building and delivery
clusters.fact: Ribosomes synthesize proteins; rough ER, smooth ER, and the Golgi divide protein processing, lipid synthesis, modification, and routing among compartments.

clusters.name: Recycling and structure
clusters.fact: Lysosomes digest selected material, peroxisomes carry out specialized oxidative reactions, and the cytoskeleton supports cell shape and internal movement.

clusters.name: Energy transformation
clusters.fact: Mitochondria use cellular respiration to generate much of a eukaryotic cell's ATP; chloroplasts in plants and algae capture light energy into chemical form.

bridges.fact: Active transport couples selective membrane movement to cellular energy, allowing substances to move against an electrochemical gradient.
Information copied from chromosomes guides protein synthesis, after which cellular machinery can fold, modify, and deliver the product.
Membrane-bound vesicles transport cargo within the endomembrane system and can fuse with the plasma membrane to release or receive material.

lenses.prompt: Which concepts are membrane-bound compartments within a eukaryotic cell?
lenses.explanation: The nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi, mitochondria, and lysosomes each enclose a specialized internal environment. Ribosomes and the cytoskeleton are cellular structures but are not membrane-bound organelles.

lenses.prompt: Which concepts directly help move selected substances across the cell boundary or between internal compartments?
lenses.explanation: Channels can permit movement down a concentration gradient, active transport can move substances against one, and Golgi-derived vesicles carry materials between compartments or toward the membrane.

lenses.prompt: Which concepts trace cellular information from stored DNA toward a protein that can be processed and delivered?
lenses.explanation: Chromosomal DNA is transcribed, ribosomes translate the resulting message, and proteins entering the endomembrane system are synthesized by ribosomes associated with the rough ER for further processing and transport.
